C is in two communities, so its edges and degree count one half in each: each community scores 2/6 - (6/12)² = 0.083, for an extended modularity of 0.167. Forcing C into one group gives a modularity of only 0.111." width="100%"} Modularity (see `modularity()`) needs each node in exactly one community. Extended modularity (Shen, Cheng, Cai & Hu, 2009) allows overlapping communities by sharing out each node: a node that belongs to `O_v` communities contributes `1 / O_v` of its degree to each, and an edge inside a community counts `1 / (O_u O_v)`: `EQ = Σ_c [ L̃_c / m - γ (D̃_c / 2m)² ]` where `L̃_c` is the discounted number of edges inside community `c`, `D̃_c` the discounted sum of its nodes' degrees, and `m` the number of edges. When the cover is a partition, this equals the ordinary modularity. On a weighted graph (`Graph(weighted=True)`) edge weights replace edge counts. The results match NetworkX's `community.overlapping_modularity()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [communities]{.doc-parameter-name} : The cover to score: a list of node groups, each a list or set of node IDs or labels. Every node must be in at least one group (see `is_cover()`); groups may overlap. A node listed twice in the same group counts once. [resolution]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The resolution parameter `γ`, as in `modularity()`. Default is `1.0`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The extended modularity of the cover. A graph without edges scores `0`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed, a node is in no group, or a label does not exist. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two triangles sharing node C: giving C to both communities scores higher than forcing it into one of them: ::: {#953f1c08 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "C")]) ) ( round(graph.overlapping_modularity([["A", "B", "C"], ["C", "D", "E"]]), 3), round(graph.overlapping_modularity([["A", "B", "C"], ["D", "E"]]), 3), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (0.167, 0.111) ``` ::: ::: Score the overlapping communities found by clique percolation: ::: {#199c0ef3 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} cover = graph.cmty_k_clique(3) round(graph.overlapping_modularity(cover), 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 0.167 ``` ::: :::
